Class DiaryEntryRegister

java.lang.Object
edu.ntnu.idi.bidata.DiaryEntryRegister
public class DiaryEntryRegister extends Object
Registry class for managing diary entries in the application.

Role and Responsibility:

The DiaryEntryRegister class is responsible for managing a collection of all DiaryEntry objects while they exist in the application. It provides functionality for:

  • Creating and storing new diary entries
  • Retrieving entries by index or through search operations
  • Searching entries by keyword, date, or date range
  • Saving/loading to/from JSON files
  • Displaying entries to the console

This class acts as the single point of access for all diary entry-related operations within the system. The register uses a Gson instance configured with a custom DiaryEntryTypeAdapter, which allowes LocalDateTime fields inside DiaryEntry objects to be correctly serialised and deserialised.

Information Stored and Data Type Justification
  • List of entries (diaryEntries): An ArrayList containing DiaryEntry objects. The type ArrayList was chosen because:
    • The number of entries starts at zero and grows dynamically as users add entries
    • Entries need to be accessed by index for editing and deletion operations
    • Iteration is required for search operations using streams
    • Easy serialisation/deserialisation with the Gson library
  • gson (Gson): A Gson instance for JSON serialisation. Gson was chosen because:
    • It handles complex object serialisation authomatically.
    • It is a widely used and well documented libary for JSON in java.
  • But Gson does not automatically support LocalDateTime. Thus a custom type adapter was required.
Mutability Assessment

The entry list and the Gson instance is created at creation of the DiaryEntryRegister object. The content of the list change, while the Gson instance is final

Invalid Data Handling Strategy

This class uses graceful degradation for I/O errors, and exception propagation for invalid indices:

  • Invalid index access: The getDiaryEntryByIndex method delegates to ArrayList.get(), which throws IndexOutOfBoundsException for invalid indices. The calling code must handle this exception.
  • Null or blank search keywords: The searchByKeyword method returns an empty list if the keyword is null or blank, allowing the application to continue without error.
  • File I/O errors: Both readFromJson and writeToJson catch IOException and print error messages to the console, allowing the application to continue running. This graceful degradation prevents crashes from file system issues.
  • Missing JSON file: The readFromJson method checks if the file exists before attempting to read, silently skipping if not found to support first-time application runs.
  • Null entries from JSON: If the JSON file contains null or invalid data, the method checks for null before adding entries to prevent errors.

  • Constructor Details

    • DiaryEntryRegister

      public DiaryEntryRegister()
      Creates a new empty DiaryEntryRegister.

      Initialises an empty list of diary entries (ArrayList) and a custom Gson instance for JSON operations which allowes LocalDateTime fields inside DiaryEntry objects to be correctly serialised and deserialised.

      Diary entries can be added via newDiaryEntry() or added from file via readFromJSON()

    • showAllEntries

      public void showAllEntries()
      Prints all diary entries to the console, togehter with their index number.

      The index corresponds to positions within the internal list. Element 0 in the list it set to be called by the index-nubmer 1 because it has the first position in the list.

      If the list of entries is empty, the text "(No entries)" is displayed.

    • addNewDiaryEntry

      public void addNewDiaryEntry(String title, Author author, String content)
      Creates a new diary entry and adds the new entry to the list diaryEntries.
      Parameters:
      title - the title of the new entry
      author - the author who created the entry (typically the author belonging to the user logged inn)
      content - the content of the new diary entry

    • searchByKeyword

      public ArrayList<DiaryEntry> searchByKeyword(String keyword)
      Searches for diary entries containing the specified keyword. The search is case-insensitive and checks the title, content, author name, and date (formatted as dd.MM.yyyy). Since it checks the title, content and date, it allowes for users to serch for words, authors or dates.
      Parameters:
      keyword - the word or phrase to search for
      Returns:
      a list of diary entries that contain the keyword

    • getEntriesBetweenDates

      public ArrayList<DiaryEntry> getEntriesBetweenDates(LocalDate startDate, LocalDate endDate)
      Returns all diary entries created between two dates (inclusive).
      Parameters:
      startDate - the start date of the range
      endDate - the end date of the range
      Returns:
      a list of diary entries within the specified date range

    • getEntriesOnDate

      public ArrayList<DiaryEntry> getEntriesOnDate(LocalDate date)
      Returns all diary entries created on a specific date.

      This method calls getEntriesBetweenDates with the same date for both start and end.

      Parameters:
      date - the date to search for
      Returns:
      a list of diary entries created on the specified date

    • readFromJson

      public void readFromJson()
      Reads diary entries from the JSON file "entries.json" into the register.

      If the file does not exist, no action is taken. This allows for a fresh start. If an I/O error occurs, an error message is printed but the application continues with any previously loaded entries.

    • writeToJson

      public void writeToJson()
      Writes all diary entries to the JSON file "entries.json".

      Overwrites any existing file content. If an I/O error occurs, an error message is printed but the application continues running.
